description: What should a parent do if they suspect their child has been injured by a vaccine? A fly-over of vaccine injury law and the federal claims process.
shortAnswer: Get your child to a doctor quickly who can diagnose the onset, and ask that doctor to document the nature of the illness, disability, injury or condition and the time period for the appearance of the first symptom after vaccine administration (this is crucial). Call a lawyer like me who can help you understand your legal options.

faq.q: Can I sue a vaccine manufacturer directly if my child was injured by a vaccine?
faq.a: Since October 1, 1988 (the effective date of the Vaccine Act) you are required to apply for compensation from the federal government prior to pursuing a lawsuit. Those with a vaccine injury from a covered vaccine cannot sue a vaccine manufacturer without first filing a claim with the U.S. Court of Federal Claims.

faq.q: What is a "table injury" under the federal vaccine injury program?
faq.a: There is a "vaccine injury table" that lists injuries that are presumed to be caused by vaccines. To show a "table injury" you have to meet one of the listings in the table and show that the injury's onset fell within the time period determined by the government.

faq.q: How much compensation does the vaccine injury program pay, and who pays the attorney fees?
faq.a: Compensation for a death resulting from vaccination is capped at $250,000. The system also will pay for past and future unreimbursed medical expenses, custodial and nursing home care; up to $250,000 for pain and suffering; and loss of earned income. Attorney fees and costs are NOT PAID BY YOU, even if your claim is unsuccessful.

faq.q: Can I bypass the federal system and bring my child's vaccine injury claim under Georgia law?
faq.a: Oh I wish it were so. In 2011 the U.S. Supreme Court nixed the Georgia Supreme Court's decision in the Ferrari case, writing that the Vaccine Act "preempts all design-defect claims against vaccine manufacturers." The law of Georgia is back in lock step with the federal system.
